history.dynasty: Kachchhapaghata dynasty - built by King Mahipala between 1090 and 1093 CE (Wikipedia, based on the inscription in the larger temple deciphered by Alexander Cunningham). One travel source (evendo.com) reports the inscription states completion around 1098 AD - conflict, verify.
history.period: 1090-1093 CE (11th century). CONFLICT: some sources say built 1093 only; inscription-dated to 1090-1093.
history.summary: The Sasbahu (Sahasrabahu) twin temples inside Gwalior Fort are 11th-century twin shrines built by King Mahipala of the Kachchhapaghata dynasty. Per Wikipedia's reading of the inscription, the larger temple ('Sas') was constructed for the king's Vaishnavite wife and is dedicated to Vishnu (the larger is dedicated to Aniruddha, grandson of Krishna, considered a Jana avatar of Vishnu in the Wikipedia article's summary); the smaller temple ('Bahu') was built for his Shiva-devotee daughter-in-law and is dedicated to Shiva. 'Sas-Bahu' is a corruption of 'Sahasrabahu' ('one with a thousand arms', an epithet of Vishnu), not literally 'mother-in-law and daughter-in-law' - though local legend repeats the family story. The tower and sanctum were destroyed in the region's invasions and Hindu-Muslim wars, so the temples stand partly in ruins; surviving are the entrance porch and mandapa on a 100 ft x 63 ft jagati platform. The larger temple was a distinctive three-storeyed structure in the North Indian Bhumija style (per art historian James Harle), with intricate carvings of deities, celestial figures and Nagara-style detailing. CSV town and state ('Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh') are correct.

name: Sasbahu Temple (Sahasrabahu Twin Temples)
town_description: The temples stand inside the Gwalior Fort complex, atop the fortified Gopachal hill overlooking Gwalior city in Madhya Pradesh, with panoramic views of the city below.

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Gwalior (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Airport) (distance not confirmed - verify).
travel.railway: Nearest railway station is Gwalior Junction; the fort is roughly 3-4 km from the station (verify).
travel.road: Inside Gwalior Fort, reached by road up the fort hill; auto-rickshaws and taxis available in Gwalior.
